# Stability

What Callisto promises to keep working from 1.0, and what it does not. A breaking change to anything in the first table needs a major version.

## Stable

| Surface | The promise |
| --- | --- |
| The eight commands (`add`, `status`, `version`, `pre`, `snapshot`, `init`, `release`, `completions`) and their flags | A flag keeps its meaning; a new flag never changes what the command did without it. |
| `--dry-run` | Accepted by every command, before or after the command name. Commands that write write nothing under it; on read-only commands it does nothing; where it cannot apply (for example `release plan`) it is a usage error. |
| Exit codes | `0` success, `1` failure, `2` usage error: a bad or missing argument or flag, including values the command validates after parsing; the same value read from `callisto.toml`, a changeset or another file is a failure, not a usage error. |
| `--format json` reports | Every report carries `schemaVersion`. Within a version a field is not removed, renamed or retyped; fields may be added. A shape change bumps the version. `release inspect` prints the intent, manifest or receipt unchanged: its own `schemaVersion`, no `command` or `dryRun`. `schema` prints JSON Schema documents, not reports. |
| `callisto.toml` | A key keeps its meaning. Unknown keys are an error, so a new key arrives in a minor release and never changes an existing file's behavior. |
| Changesets | The `.changeset/*.md` format and `pre.json` stay compatible with `@changesets/cli`. The bare package name is the key unless another ecosystem has a package of that name, in which case the key is `ecosystem/name`. |
| Error codes | A code keeps naming the same condition and is never reused. New codes may appear. |
| Tag names | `{name}@{version}` by default, `ecosystem/name@{version}` once another ecosystem has a package of that name. Pin a name with `tag-template` if a stable tag matters to your tooling. |
| The GitHub Actions | The inputs of `callisto-action` and `setup-callisto`. Only the inputs and outputs documented as supported are promised; those marked Internal are not. The floating `v1` tag moves only on stable releases; pin a commit for a fixed version. |

## CI plumbing

The generated workflows use `release plan`, `release inspect`, `release execute`, `release artifact-manifest`, `release build-python`, `release-pr`, `matrix`, `compose-pr-body` and `schema`. They are hidden from `--help` and work only with the same Callisto version that generated them: the intent, decision, receipt and run envelope carry versions, and a reader rejects any other. Keep the action and the binary on one version, and regenerate with `callisto init` after an upgrade.

`release pending` also appears in `release --help` and the release workflow uses it. Its JSON output follows the report envelope, but its flags are not part of the 1.0 CLI promise.

## Not covered

- Text output, stderr, warnings and the wording of error messages.
- The library crates (`callisto-model`, `-manifests`, `-graph`). They are internal and version in lockstep with the CLI.
- The order of keys in JSON output, and timing or performance.
- Platforms without a published binary. Windows is not supported.

VER-APPLY-14 :: By default, applying a plan refreshes and stages lockfiles for every ecosystem represented by an actual version, dependency, platform or optional-dependency write target, including all manifests of a dual-manifest package and workspace-root Cargo writes. It refreshes each existing lockfile, and creates and stages a missing `Cargo.lock`: `cargo update --workspace`, run in the directory of each Cargo workspace written to and refreshing the `Cargo.lock` beside its root manifest, for Cargo; for Pypi, `uv lock` if `uv.lock` exists, else `poetry lock --no-update` if `poetry.lock` exists, else `pdm lock --update-reuse` if `pdm.lock` exists; for Npm, `npm install --package-lock-only --ignore-scripts` for `package-lock.json`, `pnpm install --lockfile-only` for `pnpm-lock.yaml`, `yarn install --mode update-lockfile` for `yarn.lock`, and `bun install --lockfile-only` for `bun.lock` or `bun.lockb`, each independently when its lockfile is present. An npm or Python package's lockfile is the one in the workspace that owns it (the nearest directory at or above it that declares a workspace, else for a package none declares the nearest with a lockfile), and its refresh runs in that directory, so a workspace below the root keeps its own. `--no-refresh-lockfiles` skips refresh; applicable existing lockfiles are still staged. Staging takes every known lockfile of those ecosystems that exists in the owning directory, whether or not it was refreshed, except one a `.gitignore` ignores. 

VER-APPLY-19 :: Before its first write, `version` records its inputs at `refs/worktree/callisto/checkpoint/version` (`HEAD`, the index, and the workspace's working tree including untracked files, plus `HEAD`, a digest of the tags and the Callisto version), without changing the user's index or working tree and without signing. It deletes the checkpoint after its last effect, including `--emit-decision` and `--emit-preview`. A run that finds the checkpoint plans from those inputs and applies the plan to the working tree, so an interrupted run (E208, a crash, a failed emitted-file write) is finished by running `version` again and leaves the same files, index and status as a run that was never interrupted. A repository with no commits, or a plan that writes nothing, records no checkpoint. A file Git cannot read, or whose line endings `core.safecrlf` rejects, is left out of the record without stopping the run. 

VER-APPLY-20 :: A run that finds the checkpoint refuses with E340 and writes nothing when `HEAD`, the tags or the Callisto version changed since it was recorded, , when the checkpoint belongs to another workspace of the worktree, or when a file the plan was derived from (a manifest the loader opened, `callisto.toml`, a changeset) or a file it writes is on disk neither as recorded nor as the tree a finished run would leave (the plan applied to the recorded tree without a lockfile refresh), compared through Git's line-ending filters; a file the expected tree lacks counts as the run's deletion only when the index lacks it too. A dry run reports the plan without this check. The planning date and the commit history come from the recorded run. A run that cannot start (its preflight or workspace resolution fails) leaves no checkpoint. A run that cannot create the checkpoint because another run created it first fails with E341. The checkpoint belongs to one worktree. The error names the way out: delete the checkpoint ref and follow the E121 steps. 

VER-APPLY-17 :: Before the first write, every file the plan edits, creates or deletes is checked: a manifest must exist as a readable regular file, no path may be a symbolic link or sit beneath one (Git cannot stage it), no path may leave the workspace, the directory of each written file (or its nearest existing parent) must take a new file, and a file the plan stages must not be ignored by a .gitignore unless Git already tracks it. Checking creates no file or directory. Any failure stops the run with E314 naming every such path, and nothing has been written, staged or deleted. A lockfile that a .gitignore ignores is still refreshed on disk but is not staged. The checks cover only what can be known beforehand: a lockfile refresh that fails (E208) or a Git command that fails while staging can still stop the run after the writes. 

VER-APPLY-17 :: A bumped Cargo member whose version is inherited (`version.workspace = true` or `version = { workspace = true }`) gets a literal `version = "<new>"` in its own `[package]` table, in the position and with the comments of the line it replaces. `[workspace.package].version` is never written, so a member that still inherits keeps the shared version. Bumping every member of a fixed group pins each of them. 

MX-OUT-01 :: platformTargets and runtimeVersions are keyed by the package's `<ecosystem>/<name>` id for its primary ecosystem, so a cargo crate and an npm package named alike get separate entries. 

MX-OUT-02 :: Map keys are in lexicographic order, and each entry's targets are sorted by triple (cargo targets then by artifactName). 

MX-OUT-03 :: `--format json` prints pretty JSON with the standard report envelope (`command` and `dryRun`); an empty workspace prints {"schemaVersion":3,"platformTargets":{},"runtimeVersions":{},"command":"matrix","dryRun":false} and exits 0, and the diagnostics key appears only when there is at least one diagnostic. 

MX-OUT-04 :: Each target object has triple, platform, arch, abi, hostRunner, useCross, artifactName, packageDir and packageName, plus manifestPath only when set. 

MX-OUT-05 :: `--format text` and a bare `callisto matrix` print the same non-JSON table and exit 0.

Looks are spaced 15 s, 45 s, 2 minutes, then 3 minutes apart, or by the registry's `Retry-After`; no wait runs past the window. A publish whose version the registry never shows in that window fails with E157, and no receipt is written. 

REL-PUB-13 :: A registry entry may set `publish-timeout`, the longest one publish command (`cargo publish`, `npm publish`, `twine upload`) may run, as a whole number with `s`, `m` or `h` from 1 s to 1 h; the default is 15 minutes. A command that runs longer is stopped and fails with E025. The value does not enter the registry binding, so changing it does not make an earlier intent stale. A value outside that form or range is rejected when the configuration loads. 

VER-CAS-10 :: The cascade aborts with E105 when it does not settle within 4 x (package count) + 1 steps, and with a grammar-mismatch error when a spec and the new version use different version grammars (SemVer vs PEP 440). 

VER-PRE-07 :: `callisto snapshot --tag <tag>` sets every workspace package, and every attached platform package and fixed-group platform manifest, to a snapshot version built from the same tag and sha7 (the first 7 characters of HEAD) in the package's own grammar: `0.0.0-{tag}-{sha7}` for a SemVer package, `0.0.0.dev0+{tag}.{sha7}` for a Pep440 package; it fails if HEAD cannot be resolved. A snapshot version is never tagged or published: `release` refuses it with E169. 

CLI-SNAP-01 :: `callisto snapshot --tag <tag>` sets each SemVer package's manifest version to `0.0.0-<tag>-<short HEAD sha>` and each PEP 440 package's to `0.0.0.dev0+<tag>.<short HEAD sha>`, prints each `from → to`, and leaves changesets in place. A tag that is empty or has a character other than a letter, digit or `-` is rejected with E324 before anything is planned. 

VER-GRP-04 :: A package claimed by two groups is rejected: E109 when the claims use different spellings of the same package, and a group-conflict error when they use the same spelling. 

REL-PUB-04 :: PyPI publish builds with `python3 -m build --sdist --wheel --outdir <temporary directory>` in the package directory, falling back to `python` and failing with E170 when neither is on PATH, and fails with E306 when the build produced no wheel or no sdist for the version. It then runs `twine upload` naming only the built files the index lacks, with `--repository-url` for a configured upload endpoint (a registry's `publish-url`, else its `url`) and never `--skip-existing`. One build serves the preflight and the publish of a run. Every build runs with `SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH` set to the release commit's committer time. `release build-python` runs the same build for each Python publish of a plan into `--artifact-dir`.

VER-CS-04 :: Parsing fails with E040 when line 1 is not `---`, E041 when the frontmatter is never closed, and E055 when there are entries but the summary is empty or whitespace-only. A changeset with no entries and no summary (the shape `@changesets/cli add --empty` writes) parses as a valid, empty changeset. `callisto version` reports every parse failure as E210 naming the file and the parse error; the specific code is on the library error only. 

VER-CS-07 :: Writing fails for an empty summary with entries (E056), an empty package name (E057), or a name containing `"`. A changeset with no entries and no summary writes as `---`, `---` and a blank line, the shape `@changesets/cli add --empty` writes. 

REL-AUTH-05 :: `release plan` and `release execute` require the source checkout at a detached HEAD and fail with E170 otherwise. `callisto release` accepts an attached HEAD. Every route requires a complete, non-shallow SHA-1 repository and fails with E265 for a repository that is not SHA-1 and E266 for a shallow one. 

REL-AUTH-08 :: `release plan` for a source with `[release]` requires `--orchestration-revision` and `--artifact-repository` (`E231`). For a source without `[release]` it ignores both flags, prints a notice, and plans zero artifact slots. 

REL-GH-06 :: Before any effect, `release execute` fails with E139 when an artifact's bytes differ from the manifest. It fails with E140 unless `gh attestation verify` passes with the configured `--repo`, `--signer-workflow <repo>/.github/workflows/callisto-release.yml`, `--signer-digest` set to the orchestration revision, `--source-digest` and `--deny-self-hosted-runners`. 

WS-DISC-02 :: Root detection fails with E030 naming the start directory and Git toplevel when no marker or package manifest exists up to the toplevel, and with E058 (help suggests `git init`) when the start directory is not inside a Git repository. 

REL-ERR-03 :: A `[release]` section fails config loading with E197 when it has no `[[release.artifact]]`, an unsafe `target` or `asset-name`, or a duplicate `asset-name`. An unqualified `product-package` or artifact `package` fails config loading with E317 (a bare name) or E316 (the colon form). A `[release.profiles]` table is an unknown key and fails config loading. 

REL-CMD-10 :: In a workspace with `[[release.artifact]]` slots or a napi/maturin platform package, `callisto release` fails with `E239` before any effect. The help names `release plan`, `release artifact-manifest` and `release execute`. 

CLI-WF-04 :: When binaries ship as artifact slots or the workspace has napi platform packages, the generated workflow has `version-pr`, `plan` (runs `callisto release plan --from-release-commit` when the pushed commit adds or modifies .callisto/release-decision.json), `build` (a matrix from napi targets and artifact slots), `build-python` (only when the plan publishes a Python package; builds its sdist and wheel with no credentials) and `execute` (installs a pinned `twine` into a venv on the PATH when the plan publishes a Python package, runs `callisto release artifact-manifest`, sealing those files, and `callisto release execute`) jobs. The `plan`, `build-python` and `execute` jobs check out the pushed commit (`ref: ${{ github.sha }}`), not the branch, because the release commands they run require a detached HEAD (E170). Registry secrets are scoped to the execute publishing step, never plan or build; npm and Twine receive native auth configuration only during execution, and registry credentials are withheld from Python build subprocesses. Native package-manager publish hooks retain their normal package-owner-defined behavior. The build matrix and napi artifact placement cover only the packages in the release intent, so an unrelated napi addon adds no build and cannot fail the plan.

    r=subprocess.run([G,'show',tag+':docs/errors.md'],cwd=cwd,capture_output=True,text=True)

    print('  changed meaning:',len(chg))
    for c in chg[:12]: print('   ',c,'|',old[c][:70],'=>',cur[c][:70])

A runtime, optional, build or peer dependent that is itself released in this run, for any reason, has every such spec on a bumped internal dependency raised to the dependency's new version the same way, even when the spec still covers it (a covering spec that cannot be raised, such as a wildcard or a bare Python requirement, is left unchanged); a dependent that is not releasing keeps its spec unless out of range. A member's `workspace = true` entry, pnpm rolling `workspace:` shorthands and catalog specs are never rewritten in place by either rule (a Cargo `workspace = true` spec is rewritten in the root `[workspace.dependencies]`); an out-of-range pnpm explicit range is rewritten while retaining its `workspace:` protocol and alias. A dev dependent's spec is rewritten only when out of range. An npm range may carry a prerelease or build clause (`^2.0.0-next.0` becomes `^3.0.0`). A runtime, optional, build or peer spec that is out of range and cannot be rewritten mechanically, such as an npm range with spaces, `||`, a hyphen or a wildcard, or a Cargo range whose upper bound excludes the new version, fails the run with E319 before anything is written. A rewrite that would still exclude the new version, such as `<2.0.0` for 2.0.0, counts as one that cannot be rewritten. A pre-release target is not written into a caret or tilde. A spec that still covers the new version but cannot be raised is left unchanged without a diagnostic (VER-CAS-06); a runtime, optional, build or peer spec that does not cover it fails with E319; only a development dependency spec that cannot be rewritten is left unchanged with a `range-not-round-trippable` warning.

r $C release --dry-run
r $C init --yes --artifact-target x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu --forge-repository o/r --product-package cargo/app

The version is read from the package manifest or, for a Cargo package that inherits it, from the workspace manifest; files are compared by content, so a reverted change and a change made inside a merge commit count. The error names the version commit; checking it out and running `callisto release` again adopts the published version and tags that commit. CLI-STATUS-01 :: `callisto status`, with or without a callisto.toml, prints one row per package with its name, current version and planned bump (or `none`), then `<N> package(s) pending`, then a `Diagnostics:` section when any exist. 

CLI-STATUS-02 :: A package with no changeset of its own that `callisto version` would bump through dependency cascade or a fixed or linked group shows that planned bump in status and counts toward the pending total. 

CLI-STATUS-03 :: `status --format json` reports `hasChangesets`, `pending` (count of packages with a planned bump), and per package `package`, `currentVersion`, `lastReleasedVersion`, `lastTag` (null when the package has no tag), `pendingSeverity` (null when no bump is planned), `changedSinceLastTag`, `releaseTrigger` and `pendingChangesets`. `changedSinceLastTag` is true for a package with no tag, when any directory of the package holds different files than at its last tag, or when its tracked files have uncommitted changes; a change that was later reverted does not count. 

CLI-STATUS-06 :: `status --strict` reports strict-escalatable warnings as errors, so `status --check --strict` exits 1 where `status --check` exits 0. 

CLI-STATUS-07 :: `status` reports an `inferred-release-without-changeset` warning for a package whose pending release is inferred from commits and that no changeset names, because the release pull request reads changesets only; a package a changeset names, or one bumped by a dependency or group, is not reported. 

CLI-ADD-02 :: `add --format json` prints `{"schemaVersion", "command": "add", "dryRun": false, "path"}`; with --dry-run it prints `"dryRun": true`, the path and the file content, and creates no file or directory. 

CLI-ADD-03 :: `callisto add` with no --package and a terminal stdin runs a wizard asking, in order, which packages to include, which are major, which remaining are minor (the rest are patch), a non-empty summary unless --summary was given, and a final confirmation; declining the confirmation writes nothing and exits 0. Every wizard prompt and preview line prints to stderr, not stdout. 

CLI-PRE-01 :: `callisto pre enter <tag>` writes .changeset/pre.json with mode `pre`, the tag and each package's initial version; `callisto pre exit` sets its mode to `exit`. #!/bin/bash
C=/tmp/claude-501/target/debug/callisto
export GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null GIT_CONFIG_SYSTEM=/dev/null
cd /tmp/claude-501/cw
git checkout -q -- . 2>/dev/null; git clean -fdq
ls .changeset
echo "== add json"; $C add --package npm/a:patch --summary hi --format json; echo "exit $?"
echo "== add json dry"; $C add --package npm/a:patch --summary hi --format json --dry-run; echo "exit $?"
ls .changeset
echo "== status --strict"; $C status --check --strict >/dev/null 2>&1; echo "strict=$?"; $C status --check >/dev/null 2>&1; echo "nostrict=$?"
echo "== pre"
$C pre exit; echo "exit(no pre.json) $?"
$C pre enter beta >/dev/null 2>&1; echo "enter $?"

$C pre exit 2>&1 | head -3
$C pre enter rc >/dev/null 2>&1; echo "resume $?"; grep -E '"(mode|tag)"' .changeset/pre.json
git status --short | head

Verified on HEAD 1d0fe56c2 (Callisto 0.21.0). I built `callisto-cli` into /tmp/claude-501/target (not the jobs dir, which the sandbox blocks for writes), ran it in scratch repos under /tmp/claude-501, and made no repo edits.

**Counts.** I checked 65 criteria across all five spec files (cli 22, matrix 5, release 14, versioning 14, workspace 10) against code and the binary.
- True: 61
- Partly true: 2 (REL-ERR-02, VER-APPLY-17)
- False: 0
- Unverifiable here: 2
  - WS-LOAD-01: I could not trigger E313. An unreadable member manifest gives a discovery warning, which WS-DISC-09 allows.
  - REL-GH-06: no real GitHub attestation run. I read the code, and its argv matches the spec.

I also mechanically checked all 100 criteria that cite E-codes. 132 distinct codes appear and every one is in the registry. The one exception is `E404` in REL-PUB-07, which is npm's own code.

**Partly true (the first two are doc hygiene; the third is not a criterion defect).**
- REL-ERR-02 lists E216, E217 and E218 for `--dry-run`. `release build-python --dry-run` also exits 2, with E309, and the criterion omits it. Fix: add `build-python/E309`.
- VER-APPLY-17 is used for two different criteria, one on preflight and one on inherited Cargo versions. Fix: renumber one.
- VER-APPLY-20 has a stray `, ,` in the text.
- `init --yes --artifact-target` with no `origin` exits 1 with E299, before E241, E195 or E196. CLI-INIT-09 states this without the code, so CLI-INIT-10 and -12 are right as written.

**What was true.**
- The matrix JSON claim (MX-OUT-03) holds: the report has `schemaVersion` 3, `command` and `dryRun`.
- VER-APPLY-14: every refresh command in the spec matches `apply.rs`.
- VER-APPLY-19 and -20: the checkpoint ref name, E340 and E341 match the code, and `version_resume_tests` pass.
- Every exit-2 versus exit-1 claim I tried held, for E316, E317, E102, E169, E270 and E274.

**docs/stability.md "Stable" table: all rows true today.**
- The eight commands match `--help`.
- `--dry-run` is accepted before and after every command. `release plan --dry-run` exits 2 (E217).
- Exit codes: a bad `--package` exits 2. A colon-form package in a changeset exits 1. An unknown key in `callisto.toml` exits 1 (E325).
- `schemaVersion` is present on status, snapshot, version, matrix, add, pre, init, release (5), release pending and the error envelope.
- Unknown keys error, including `[release.profiles]`.
- Error codes: the seven retired codes (E008, E050, E248, E253, E254, E257, E258) are absent from code and listed as retired in docs/errors.md. Nothing else dropped out of the registry since 0.10.0. Some meanings were widened (E121, E233, E276) but none repurposed.
- Tag names: the default is `{name}@{version}`, and `tag_name_contract_tests` and `identity_promotion_tests` pass.

**docs/errors.md versus code.** There are 278 codes on each side, with no diff and no duplicates. `crates/callisto-graph/tests/error_registry_architecture.rs` already enforces both directions plus unique numeric codes. It passes.

**Tests run, all exit 0:** `error_registry_architecture`, `error_envelope_tests`, `version_resume_tests`, `dry_run_invariant_tests`, `output_flags_conformance`, `error_code_hygiene_tests`, `tag_name_contract_tests`, `identity_promotion_tests` and `add_duplicate_package_tests`. I did not run the full suite, clippy or the repo's other check commands.

**Drift estimate.** The 14% figure no longer holds. I found 0 false and about 3% with minor omissions or typos, and the E-code, matrix `command` and VER-APPLY-14 items from the October review all check out now. This is a 65-criterion sample out of 262 criteria, chosen mostly toward code-checkable claims. I read only the first part of some of the longest criteria in full (REL-PR-10, REL-RERUN-07), so the true rate could be a few points higher.
